root_cause.text: The oplock/lease break notifier functions read `opinfo->conn` without either `READ_ONCE()` or a NULL check, allowing a concurrent SMB2 LOGOFF to set `op->conn` to `NULL` after `ci->m_lock` is dropped, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when `ksmbd_conn_r_count_inc()` writes through the NULL pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states: "smb2_oplock_break_noti() and smb2_lease_break_noti() read opinfo->conn into a local with neither READ_ONCE() nor a NULL check. ... a concurrent SMB2 LOGOFF (session_fd_check()) can set op->conn = NULL under ci->m_lock within that window. ksmbd_conn_r_count_inc(conn) then writes through NULL at offset 0xc4 -- a remotely triggerable oops." The patch addsis `conn = READ_ONCE(opinfo->conn); if (!conn) return 0;` before use.
